newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DOE to release products reserve study in fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DOE to release products reserve study in fall.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department will release its final version of a study on establishing regional reserves for petroleum products in late summer or early fall, a department spokesman said Thursday.

Rep. Joseph Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat pushing the idea of federal reserves for oil products, in a letter called on the department to give him drafts of the study and complained that it was supposed to be completed by April.

"I am concerned that the delay in providing its report to Congress reflects continued DOE adherence to this policy (of opposing a products reserve) and that an unbiased and complete presentation of findings may be in jeopardy," Kennedy wrote to Energy Secretary Federico Pena.
"I am writing to you because of concerns that there may be attempts to alter or discount positive findings in the study," Kennedy said.
The spokesman said the department was preparing a response to Kennedy.
Several Northeast lawmakers raised the idea of a reserve for oil products last winter when prices soared for heating oil, heavily used in the Northeast to heat homes.
Kennedy and others said establishing regional reserves of products could work to stabilize prices, under the same theory that the nation keeps the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The department spokesman said the products reserve study will be released at the same time the department issues a study on the future of SPR.
